findings.title: deleteCache rejects team/delegation credentials and throws generic Error
findings.body: The handler only accepts credentials whose `userId` equals the session user, so calendar credentials owned by a team (userId null, teamId set) or delegation-derived credentials can never have their cache cleared, even though the UI renders the "Delete cached data" item for them (the dropdown only checks `delegationCredentialId` for the disconnect action, not for cache deletion). It also throws a plain `Error` instead of a `TRPCError({ code: "FORBIDDEN"/"NOT_FOUND" })`, which surfaces as a 500 internal error and leaks the message as an unexpected server failure instead of a proper authorization response.

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data object
findings.body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` issues a Prisma `updateMany` with an empty `data` payload. Prisma does not guarantee that an empty update bumps `@updatedAt` (and for some providers it is a no-op / can error), so the stated intent ("Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt") is not reliably achieved. Pass `{ updatedAt: new Date() }` explicitly. Additionally, for in-memory delegation credentials `this.credential.id` can be negative/non-existent, making this an unnecessary write on every cache refresh. The PR description itself notes this field isn't consumed anywhere in the UI, so it may be dead work.

findings.title: Cache status ignores expiresAt, so expired cache shown as valid
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` aggregates `MAX(updatedAt)` for all `CalendarCache` rows of a credential with no filter on `expiresAt`. Rows that have already expired (and are therefore never served) still produce a `cacheUpdatedAt` value, so the UI reports an active cache and a "Last updated" time for credentials whose cache is effectively dead. Filter on `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` (or surface expiry separately).

findings.title: Repository instantiated directly, bypassing calendar-cache feature gating
findings.body: The handler constructs `CalendarCacheRepository` directly instead of going through `CalendarCache.init(...)`, which is the path that returns `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` when the calendar-cache feature is disabled. This adds an unconditional DB `groupBy` on every connectedCalendars request even for installations/teams where calendar cache is off, and bypasses the mock abstraction the interface was designed for.

findings.title: deleteCache mutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars query
findings.body: The disconnect mutation invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `viewer.apps.integrations`, but `deleteCacheMutation` only calls the optional `onSuccess` prop. When `onSuccess`/`onChanged` isn't supplied (it is optional and is undefined in some call sites), the UI keeps showing the old `cacheUpdatedAt` after a successful delete, suggesting the cache still exists. Invalidate `connectedCalendars` in the mutation's `onSettled`.

findings.title: Timestamp hardcoded to en-US locale and browser timezone
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` ignores the user's selected locale and time format preference, so non-English users see a US-formatted date inside otherwise translated text. Use the app locale (available via `useLocale`) and the user's `timeFormat`/timezone settings.

findings.title: Script uses macOS-only sed syntax and a fragile relative .env path
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD/macOS syntax; on GNU/Linux `sed -i ''` interprets the empty string as the script argument and fails, so the GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL rewrite silently errors for Linux contributors. Also `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is relative to the invocation directory, so running the script from the repo root writes/creates a `.env` one level above the repository.

findings.title: dev:cron switched to npx tsx without adding tsx dependency
findings.body: `dev:cron` now runs `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but `tsx` is not listed in dependencies/devDependencies (while the now-unused `ts-node` remains). `npx` will attempt an unpinned network install at run time, which fails offline/CI and gives a non-reproducible version. Add `tsx` as a devDependency (and drop `ts-node` if no longer used).

findings.title: Migration warning comment contradicts the statement
findings.body: The generated warning block says "Added the required column `updatedAt` ... without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty", but the actual statement does add `DEFAULT NOW()`. Leaving the stale warning is misleading to anyone reviewing migration history; remove or correct it.
